ayahOccurrences.text: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّهُمْ فِى كُلِّ وَادٍ يَهِيمُونَ
ayahOccurrences.highlightedHtml: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّهُمْ فِى كُلِّ وَادٍ يَهِيمُونَ

lexSnapshot.derivativeNote: يَهِيمُونَ is in the derivative form: يَهِيمُ
lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
هـ/ي/م   h–y–m to wander about aimlessly, to be confused, to be bewildered, to be puzzled, to be robbed of the senses; to be infatuated, to be enchanted, to be carried away; to be demented by thirst, a waterless desert.

Of this root, 2 forms occur 1 time each in the Qur’an:
يَهِيمُ yahım and هِيمٌ hım.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
يَهِيمُ yahım [imperf. of v. هَامَ hāma, intrans.] to wander about, to roam, to drift, to ramble senselessly

(26:225) أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّهُمْ فِى كُلِّ وَادٍ يَهِيمُونَ do you not see how they meander around every subject [lit. in every valley]?

entries.label: هِيمٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
هِيمٌ hım [pl. of act. part. أَهْيَمُ ʾahyam or هَائِم hāʾim] (of camels) confused or demented (through thirst)

(56:55) فَشَارِبُونَ شُرْبَ الْهِيمِ drinking [it] like the drinking of thirst‐demented camels.
